describes: What this pack's houses were painted with and how they were kept: the colours (NCS codes and the sRGB they print as), the colours each period chose for each part of a house, the paint system of each period (materials/paint-*.json says how each ages), and the care rule that repaints a house from its wealth and its dated events. tools/houses.py walks each house's life by these to its coats on the date; the house shader reads the coats. Nothing here is a dated event: a repaint the care rule makes shows no year a player can read (docs/facts-contract.md, Keepers and care).

care.neglect: an event 'neglected' with amount a (per mille) from its year lengthens every later interval by 1 / (1 - a/1000); 'boarded' over the whole house stops repainting until 'unboarded'; 'restored' and 'repainted' put on a coat in their year
care.windowsNew: a window put in by an event 'windows_replaced' comes painted in its year, in the period's window colour

notes.weather: How much harder a coat weathers where it is most exposed, as a share more: a wall facing south (sun), the lowest footM of a wall (splash; paint fails first on the lowest boards), a board's lap edge (water stands on it), falling off fast above it; under a sill's run-off and at a board's end grain (timber.json, marks); a wall facing the driving rain (from rainFromDeg, south-west: the research's weather wall, south and west, unverified for the town's winds, house-fronts.md). Each board a little its own (boardSpread), and the wall in patches about patchM across (patchSpread: how well each coat took, claiming nothing; round 4, so the failure gathers into patches with whole paint between, as on the archive's neglected fronts), less than the exposure so the failure follows the water: a film paint holds on the open wall for its onsetYears, and goes two to three times sooner where water works in, which is when a house is due its repaint. The research's order of failure; the numbers judged by look.
notes.colours: The Stavanger colour guide's NCS codes (reviews/lt1/houses/first-pass/research-subject.md, 2. Paint); their sRGB as plan-home.com prints each NCS S code (fetched 27 October 2026), a screen value, to check against an NCS fan deck. Stavangerblaa is the guide's NCS S 7020-R90B.
notes.periods: The research's colours by period: before about 1850 white was dear, so white fronts and red or ochre backs ('back') with dark windows; 1850-84 ochres, browns, white and grey with dark windows and contrasting trims; 1884-1910 whites and greys; 1910-40 green trims, white with blue; from 1945 alkyd brought pastels, dark red and blue, with white windows. Doors most often green, otherwise blue-black, red or brown. From 1990 (this pack's assumption, so a house can be walked to a later date): the old town's whites and the period colours the colour guide recommends again, with white or dark windows. Which colour of a period's list a house took is drawn from its seed. A 'back' of null paints the back as the body.
notes.schemes: Inside Gamle Stavanger a rule chose the colour: from the preservation scheme of 1956 the quarter was all white, with white windows (research-subject.md, 2. Paint; the town's script, 1956: the old town protected). Its houses are the fixture's placements on lanes (the corner and the hill round it, all in the old town by the town plan). Under a scheme a coat keeps a part's colour while it is one the scheme allows, so a repaint in the same white reads the same white; a part not yet in one takes the period's draw if the scheme allows it, else the scheme's first. Which whites count as white is this pack's reading of the colour guide's whites. Doors are free.
notes.soil: Dirt and green growth (algae) gather on a coat in a wet town where water runs and stands: by how much more water works in than on the open wall (the weather's foot, lap edge and sill run-off, paint.json weather; not end grain, which drinks water in but holds none on the face), and openShare of that on the open wall, so an old white coat stays chalky-pale in the open and goes grey-green at the foot, under the sills and in the laps; up to most of the way to a grey-green, perDecade at full weather, slowly at first while the growth takes hold and then fast (common knowledge of painted timber in a wet climate, assumed; judged by look). A new coat is clean; so a coat's years read on the wall (round 3: 0.6 and 0.35 over the whole weather left a 7-year coat 5% from a 2-year one in drizzle, and 1.0 and 0.45 tarred a 22-year wall; round 4: 1.6 with the slow start sets a 2-year coat clean, a 7-year one grey under its sills and in its laps, and leaves a 22-year open wall pale).
notes.systems: Linseed oil paint was the rule until about 1960; alkyd oil paint (Drygolin) from 1948 and pure alkyd from the early 1960s; acrylic beside alkyd from the 1960s, never dated as the usual choice (the research). 1950 as the switch and acrylic's quarter share from 1975 are this pack's assumptions.
notes.care: Repainted every 8-15 years, the south wall more often (the research): intervalYears runs from a house of wealth 0 (15) to one of 1000 (8), each interval drawn within intervalJitter of it, so a house nobody neglects never wears a coat much past 15 years. A care repaint chooses its colours again from its own period at recolourShare (the research: colour follows the repaint's date; 0.5 an assumption), otherwise it matches the faded coat; a dated repaint always chooses again, a restoration never. lapFactor 0.8 put every lap edge of a kept nine-year alkyd coat past its onset (the strict review, 27 October): 0.3, the lap³ still gathering the loss at the edges. boardSpread: one board's paint fails up to that share ahead of or behind the mean (sapwood against heartwood, each board's seed); without it a neglected wall flaked evenly, like spots (round 2, judged by look).
